A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DICE for monocular hand-face interaction and deformation recovery. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DICE benchmark results, contact-estimation results, ablations, and qualitative reconstructions in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated comparators, quantitative ablation results, and qualitative failure examples.

M1.justification: The HRNet backbone, MeshNet/InteractionNet branches, IKNets, FLAME/MANO outputs, and depth/adversarial weak supervision remain unchanged. Sections 3 and Appendices A/C clarify the existing architecture and losses without establishing a changed DICE procedure.

E1.justification: The Decaf, 500-image in-the-wild, RenderMe-360, and FreiHand coverage is retained. Figure 9 adds qualitative failure cases involving an infant and a fully occluded face, extending the represented population and input conditions while retaining the two earlier examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all earlier comparators and adds PIXIE-R, trained with DICE losses, and a single-target FastMETRO variant using independent hand and face networks. These additions substantially strengthen the task-adapted regression comparison beyond the earlier PIXIE whole-body and modified METRO baselines.

E3.justification: The added comparisons introduce loss-matched PIXIE-R training and FastMETRO training with DICE's hyperparameters, losses, and optimizer. Existing DICE settings remain unchanged, including the subject/view split already specified in v1 Appendix A.4, training budget, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds quantitative support for the intermediate-vertex-supervision ablation already discussed in v1. Figure 7 removes one depth-ablation example, while Figure 9 adds two failure cases. The principal ablation questions and depth-supervision analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical results. Both retain single-value reporting.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and contact-estimation scores remain unchanged. Table 1 adds PIXIE-R and FastMETRO PVE values of 11.0 and 9.27; Table 3 adds the intermediate-supervision ablation results 12.2/14.4/11.1/70.7 for PVE/MPJPE/PAMPJPE/F-score. Collision-distance, non-collision, and touchness breakdowns for the ablations are removed. The runtime comparison changes from more than 700x to more than 200x, consistent with the retained timings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and loss equations in Section 3.3 and Appendix C remain substantively unchanged. Distribution symbols and parameter notation are clarified, but no new mathematical derivation, formal result, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: first end-to-end deformation-aware hand-face recovery, improved generalization through weak supervision, superior reconstruction, and interactive inference at 20 fps. The added comparisons support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses optimization-based methods' higher plausibility and computational cost, and attributes the slight F-score decrease with in-the-wild training to distribution differences. It adds explanations about depth correspondence under misalignment, hand deformation as future work, broader failure conditions, and task-specific demographic-bias and misuse concerns in Appendix D.3.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the generic future code-release promise with a specific repository address, without establishing that code is already available. It documents the new comparator adaptations and training controls and clarifies contact-metric computation. Most architecture, hardware, hyperparameter, and split details were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds the decoupled-weight-decay reference and removes LaserHuman. It also describes Decaf as the previous state of the art rather than the first and only method. The broader related-work discussion and DICE's positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and method exposition undergo substantial rewriting, including an explicit three-design narrative and clearer descriptions of intermediate meshes and weak supervision. The experimental narrative expands the baseline descriptions and reorganizes the ablation discussion. Author-year citations, updated affiliations, acknowledgments, and a societal-impact subsection further revise the document presentation.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reorganized into optimization and regression comparison groups, and Table 3 gains a row while losing three metric columns. Figure 7 is reduced from three examples to two; Figure 9 expands from two examples to four in a grid. The ICLR template changes headers and typography, while the principal schematics and most qualitative figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The task-adapted baselines in Table 1 and numerical support for the previously discussed ablation strengthen the empirical argument. Clearer plausibility tradeoffs, expanded failure cases, and the corrected runtime comparison improve transparency. These gains outweigh the lost ablation diagnostics, but the improvement is limited: the new claim of a 27% PVE reduction over PIXIE-R conflicts with Table 1's 11.0 versus 8.32, which implies about 24.4%.
